verdict.summary: Correct, but each minute re-scans the whole grid instead of expanding from the rotten frontier.
missed_edge_cases: A grid with no fresh oranges should return 0 even if there are no rotten ones.

failing_inputs.input: 100x100 grid with one rotten orange in a corner

tier1.summary: Same simulation, but stop as soon as a pass rots nothing and avoid copying the grid.

line_comments.comment: Track the fresh count so you can exit early.

tier2.approach: Collect rotten cells once per minute instead of scanning every cell.
tier2.what_changes: Keep a list of cells that rotted last minute and only look at their neighbours.
tier2.why_faster: Each cell is processed a constant number of times.

tier3.insight: Every rotten orange spreads at the same speed, so a multi-source BFS gives the minute each cell rots.

tier4.notes: Use a flat array index r*W+c and a fixed dx/dy table; process the queue level by level.
tier4.interview_caveat: Flattened indices are harder to read aloud; explain the mapping first.
